scheduler-vllm.d: The EngineCore component that, at every step, decides how many tokens each request processes (within the token and sequence budgets), admits requests from the queue, and preempts when the KV cache runs out.

engine-core.d: The vLLM V1 process that runs the main loop: schedule() → execute_model() → update_from_output(), one step after another.

static-batching.d: Forming a batch of requests and running it until all of them finish before accepting new ones. The slots of requests that finish early sit idle.

continuous-batching.d: Iteration-level scheduling: the batch is re-decided at every step; a request that finishes leaves and its slot is refilled in the next step.

max-num-seqs.d: Ceiling on the number of requests active in the scheduler at the same time (slots). Beyond it, requests wait in the WAITING queue. It also influences CUDA graph sizes and buffers.

max-num-batched-tokens.d: Token budget per step, adding up decodes (including speculative drafts) and prefill chunks. It also sizes activation profiling and several buffers.

verify-rows.d: Positions processed in a speculative decode step: sequences × (1 + k). They define the size of the decode batch and the CUDA graph sizes to capture.

uniform-decode.d: A step in which every request is in decode with the same query length (1, or 1 + k with speculation). It is the case that a FULL CUDA graph can replay.

head-of-line-blocking.d: When a large item at the front (a huge prefill) prevents the small items behind it from being served, increasing everyone's wait.

chunked-prefill.d: Slicing a prompt's prefill into chunks that share each step with the decodes, instead of processing it all at once.

long-prefill-threshold.d: --long-prefill-token-threshold: ceiling on the prefill tokens a single request gets per step (0 = no ceiling). Unlike MNBT, which is the ceiling for the whole step.

decode-starvation.d: Requests in decode that get zero tokens per step because prefills in front of them consumed the budget. In V1 they are skipped, not preempted — which is why they do not show up as preemptions.

partial-prefill.d: An admitted request whose prompt has not finished processing yet (num_computed_tokens < num_prompt_tokens). DeepSeek's issue #27 caps how many of them can exist at the same time.

decode-floor.d: A guarantee of minimum service per step for each active decode: when a prefill chunk is scheduled, budget is reserved for the decodes behind it (DeepSeek hotfix #43).

fairness-spread.d: The ratio between the worst and the best stream in a burst (TTFT or decode rate). It reveals starvation that aggregate throughput hides; it is the criterion of DeepSeek's gate26.

mixed-step.d: A step that contains decodes and a prefill chunk at the same time. It is not uniform, it leaves the FULL decode CUDA graph and, on some backends, it costs seconds.

service-time-fairness.d: Splitting the engine's time (not its tokens) between the requests that are decoding and the one doing prefill: a credit accrues a fraction of the time and pays for mixed turns. It is GLM's fair v5 policy.

aging.d: An anti-starvation rule in schedulers: the longer a request waits without service, the higher its chance of being served.

preemption.d: When KV blocks run out, the scheduler removes a request (the lowest-priority one), frees its blocks and sends it back to the queue; in RECOMPUTE mode it redoes its prefill when it comes back.

oversubscription.d: Offering ceilings (context × slots) whose sum exceeds the KV pool, counting on the actual sum of live tokens fitting almost all the time. When it does not fit, preemption happens.

output-placeholder.d: A position reserved for a token that the step in flight has yet to produce (or a still-unknown draft, marked as -1) under async scheduling.

serving-profile.d: A coherent combination of maximum context, slots, token budget and scheduler policies, validated by measurements for a given type of workload.

chunk-ou-rodada.d: Iteration rule of TensorFold's multi-stream scheduler (GLM·TF recipe): each iteration runs a prompt chunk or a decode round, never both in the same forward. A credit counted in iterations (TF_GLM_FILL_SHARE, default 0.5) decides when a chunk goes in.

janela-em-lote.d: The verification windows (pending token + drafts) of every stream in a round, side by side in a single forward. In TensorFold, up to 16 rows per stream and 32 in total in v1.3.2 (64 by default with PARALLEL above 4 since v1.5), with one CUDA graph for each row count.

multi-prefill.d: Putting the next rows of several prompts in the same prompt chunk: the row-independent work (projections, experts) runs once for all of them, and what depends on each stream's state runs piece by piece. In TensorFold, MULTI_PREFILL=1.

shortest-remaining-first.d: A classic scheduling policy (shortest remaining processing time): serve first whoever has the least work left, which reduces the average wait. TensorFold's multi-prefill uses it to order the prompts inside a chunk.

fill-fatiado.d: In the GLM·TF recipe since v1.4 (patch 0062): while other streams decode, a new prompt's chunk runs a few layers at a time (about FILL_BUDGET_MS = 200 ms per slice), with a decode round between slices. Replies already streaming stop freezing; the new prompt arrives a little later.

streaming-suave.d: Sending a streamed reply's tokens one event at a time, at a steady pace, from a small playout buffer (400 ms in the GLM·TF recipe, patch 0061): drafted bursts and short pauses don't show on the wire, at the cost of text arriving that much later.
